about: MEASURED ANE embedding fast path (M1 Pro, macOS 26.5.1, coremltools 9.0, 2026-07-28). The shipped Core ML bge-small-en-v1.5 graph is a fixed (1,512) shape; this measures a second (1,128) graph for short text. Real device measurements, not estimates.

finding_1_padding_does_not_help.note: The (1,512) graph costs the same regardless of how many REAL tokens it holds - masking padding saves nothing, because the graph always computes 512 positions.

finding_2_sequence_sweep.note: Each length converted fresh, 60 iterations, p50 ms. 128 is a distinct OPTIMUM, not merely 'shorter is faster' - 96 and 160 are both ~2.5x slower than it.

finding_3_equivalence.note: CORRECTED. An earlier version of this file reported cos_128_vs_512 = 0.999097 and called that the 512 graph's own run-to-run noise floor. Both halves of that were wrong: 0.999097 was an UNNORMALIZED dot product (these vectors are not exactly unit-norm in FP16, so a raw dot understates agreement), and the 512 graph is not noisy at all - two identical runs are BIT-identical, so its noise floor is exactly 0. Re-measured properly, the real result is stronger than the claim it replaces.

mixed_space_check.why: the decisive production case: a corpus already STORED from the 512 graph, queried with vectors freshly embedded on the 128 graph

finding_4_end_to_end.note: Through the real CoreMLEmbedder.embed() with both graphs cached.

workload_justification.conclusion: Queries and facts fit 128 comfortably; document chunks (1200 chars) do NOT, so the fast graph is used ONLY when the tokenized text genuinely fits. No input is ever truncated by this optimization.

ane_utilization.note: Core ML compute plan for the shipped graph, excluding const (weight) ops.
ane_utilization.cpu_residue: input-embedding stage (gather, first layer_norm, casts) - a known Core ML pattern, not a defect
